label: hook-owned idle liquidity yield
summary: Plan a hook that places otherwise idle pool inventory into a pinned yield vault while preserving solvency, recall, losses, and user exits.
requiredFacts: Exact vault standard, asset, share math, source, revision, deployment, runtime, fees, limits, pause, upgrade, governance and loss behavior
Which pool-owned inventory may leave PoolManager accounting, who authorizes it, and how every asset and share liability is namespaced by PoolId
Liquidity buffer, withdrawal queue, recall trigger, maximum delay, failed recall, partial recall, vault loss and insolvency allocation
Yield beneficiary, Programmable and project fee separation, compounding, rounding, dust, donation and emergency exit policy
Router, quote and partial-fill behavior while inventory is deployed or recall is unavailable
requiredFiles: Pinned vault and hook dependency closure
Asset, share and PoolId liability model
Recall, loss, pause, retirement and user-exit state machine
Keeper and monitoring contract when automation is required
Executable fork or exact local vault integration tests
requiredTests: Deposit, withdrawal, preview mismatch, share-price donation, rounding, fee, cap, pause, upgrade and malicious vault behavior
Swap and liquidity demand before, during and after full, partial, delayed and failed recall
Vault loss, zero shares, insolvent inventory, emergency exit, retirement and no cross-pool liability leakage
All four swap quadrants, partial fills, quote-to-execution parity and final zero PoolManager deltas
Keeper outage, duplicate trigger, reorg, gas spike, unauthorized caller and monitoring alert
risks: Vault shares are not guaranteed to redeem one-for-one and may be paused, capped, upgraded or impaired
Deployed inventory can make swaps or withdrawals unavailable exactly when liquidity is most valuable
Combining PoolManager deltas, underlying assets and vault shares can hide insolvency or cross-pool leakage
